cohort_name: unnamed: Early Psychosis Prevention and Intervention Centre (EPPIC), Orygen, north-west Melbourne, 2011-2016
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV; diagnosis made by the treating consultant psychiatrist at three months after service entry and reviewed at discharge
diagnosis_confirmed: clinical diagnosis by treating consultant psychiatrist, reviewed at discharge; no research diagnostic interview
overlap_notes: Distinct from eppic_melbourne_1998 (conus2017) and from eppic_ips_rct (killackey2019): same service, different and non-overlapping registration windows. This cohort is all clients registered 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2016.
employment_selection_verbatim: All eligible clients registered with EPPIC between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2016 were included. To be eligible for EPPIC, clients must be between 15 and 24 years of age, reside within the catchment area, and have experienced FEP, defined as experiencing full-threshold psychotic symptoms daily for at least one week. Sources of referral include local mental health services, general practitioners, law enforcement agencies, community support services, family members and friends, and self-referral. All psychotic disorders were included, including drug-induced psychotic disorder. | 'As it was essential to ensure that all cases of first episode of psychosis were included and therefore the cohort would be representative, a waiver of individual consent was granted.'
employment_selection_source: Methods, Participants, p. 1390; Methods, Setting, p. 1390; Methods, Ethical approval, p. 1391

cohort_name: unnamed: PROESQ (Universidade Federal de Sao Paulo) and CAISM (Santa Casa de Sao Paulo) outpatient schizophrenia services, Sao Paulo, 2012-2013
diagnostic_instrument: DSM-IV criteria for schizophrenia applied by the referring psychiatrists
diagnosis_confirmed: referring psychiatrist's clinical diagnosis; no structured diagnostic interview reported
employment_selection_verbatim: All individuals undergoing treatment in the Schizophrenia Program (Programa de Esquizofrenia - PROESQ) of Universidade Federal de Sao Paulo (UNIFESP) and the Integrated Center for Mental Health (Centro de Atencao Integrada a Saude Mental - CAISM) of Santa Casa de Sao Paulo who expressed a desire for employment were invited by their psychiatrist to participate in the study. | 'A convenience sample was formed of 53 of schizophrenics desiring employment, each of whom was followed up for 18 months.' | 'All prospective participants were interviewed and allocated into groups for prevocational training. ... Those who had participated in at least 6 meetings were included in the study.' | 'All participants (n=53) completed the prevocational training group, produced a new resume and acquired the necessary documentation to be hired for a formal job.'
employment_selection_source: Materials and methods, Participants, p. 36; Materials and methods, Prevocational training, p. 37

cohort_name: unnamed: Brooklyn Community Services vocational rehabilitation programmes (Project Moving On, MetroClub, Adult Rehabilitation Services), Brooklyn NY, 2005-2009
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID) at baseline; severe mental illness as defined by the State of New York
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID administered by trained interviewers at baseline
overlap_notes: Distinct from the earlier supported-employment non-responder trial by the same group (McGurk et al. 2015, Am J Psychiatry 172:852-861), which this report cites as a separate study of non-responders to high-fidelity supported employment.
employment_selection_verbatim: Inclusion criteria for the study were: a) SMI, as defined by the State of New York (18 years of age or older; DSM-IV Axis I diagnosis other than drug or alcohol use disorders, organic brain syndromes, developmental disability or social condition; receiving Social Security Supplemental Income/Social Security Disability Income due to a specific mental illness; extended impairment in functioning due to mental illness; and reliance on psychiatric treatment, rehabilitation, and supports; b) currently enrolled in a vocational rehabilitation program for at least 3 months; c) has not benefited from recent vocational rehabilitation, defined as either has not worked for the past 3 months, including transitional employment jobs, or having a recent unsuccessful ending of a job (being fired or ending the job without another job in place) that lasted less than 3 months; and d) willing to sign informed consent to participate in the study.

cohort_name: unnamed: community mental health clinics affiliated with the New York State Psychiatric Institute; recruitment years not reported
diagnostic_instrument: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID), administered by master's-level staff
diagnosis_confirmed: SCID-based DSM-IV diagnosis; raters had inter-rater reliability of 0.78 for symptom interviews
overlap_notes: COHORT SLUG QUERY, not resolved here. The slug institute_living_rct and the author affiliations point to The Institute of Living at Hartford Hospital, Connecticut, but the report itself says participants 'were recruited from community mental health clinics affiliated with the New York State Psychiatric Institute' and that 'The New York State Psychiatric Institute Institutional Review Board approved the study'. The slug is left unchanged because the batch ledger and manifest key on it; the discrepancy is recorded in manifest_changes.csv and unresolved_queries.md.
employment_selection_verbatim: Sixty-four participants with schizophrenia-spectrum disorders who were deemed not ready for supported employment by their referring clinician due to their symptoms, poor employment history, and/or cognitive impairments were recruited from community mental health clinics affiliated with the New York State Psychiatric Institute. More specifically, the vocational counselors at the clinics had informed the referring clinician that the participant was not ready for supported employment due to (a) acute or recurring positive symptoms ...; (b) history of no placement or unsuccessful placement in the past 6 months; (c) poor performance in work assessment ...; and (d) participant reporting he or she did not feel ready to look for work. Referral typically included all of the above, with no placement or no history of success in past 6 months the requisite. That is, all of the referrals to the study met that criterion according to the vocational counselors. | 'All participants were enrolled in a four-month work therapy program ... Each participant was enrolled in a work placement for up to 10 h a week'

cohort_name: RADAR (Research into Antipsychotic Discontinuation and Reduction) trial
diagnostic_instrument: clinical diagnosis of schizophrenia or recurrent non-affective psychotic disorder; instrument not stated in this report (trial methods published separately)
diagnosis_confirmed: trial eligibility diagnosis; Table 1 splits the cohort into schizophrenia 174/253 and other psychotic disorders 79/253
overlap_notes: Secondary analysis of the RADAR trial (ISRCTN90298520, NCT03559426). The main trial report is cited as reference 33 of this paper and is a separate publication; if that report is in the review it shares these participants and the result-selection rule applies.
employment_selection_verbatim: Briefly, participants were aged 18 years and above and had a diagnosis of recurrent non-affective psychotic disorder, for which they were prescribed antipsychotic medication. The exclusion criteria included an admission to a psychiatric hospital or a mental health crisis within the preceding month, being mandated to take their medication through the Mental Health Act and being considered to pose a serious risk to themselves or others by their treating clinicians. Written, informed consent was obtained from all participants, who were then randomised to receive either maintenance antipsychotic treatment or an individualised dose reduction regimen.
